name: Jalanie George
strengths: George chases from sideline to sideline with a relentless EDGE motor — tracks sweeps across the field and still finishes with burst.
George uses violent hands to rake at the ball in pursuit and punch-rip off blockers instead of getting washed.
George bends the arc for a 6-5 frame — dips the shoulder, flattens, and keeps pad level through contact on early wins.
George stacks with length at the point of attack, creates separation, and stays gap-sound vs zone before disengaging.
weaknesses: George needs a fuller counter package when tackles get hands on him early — speed alone will stall vs Power-4 OT.
George still rises into contact on some run snaps; pad-level consistency and added mass are the next polish items.
comparison: George comps to Will Anderson Jr. — listed 6-5 / 240 vs Anderson’s ~6-4 / 243 EDGE mold (height within ~1", same long-limb rusher frame); then matching pursuit, bend, and early production traits (size-matched; not a Florida-alum default).
projection: George projects to develop into Florida’s EDGE room with Year-1 special-teams / sub-package rush snaps, Year-2 compete for a rotational every-down role, and Year-3+ starter upside as a multi-front edge who can set the edge and win 1-on-1s if he adds functional mass while keeping the bend.
schemeFit: George fits a multiple front that wants a long JACK/BUCK who can rush, set the edge, and run twist games without bailing on backside pursuit.
staffNotes: FILM VERIFIED 2026-08-09 from Desert Edge sophomore highlights (Jalanie George #90, ~4:21). Watched full package — pursuit, bend, hands, and gap discipline stand out; counters + pad level still polish.
recruitingStory: Jalanie George is a 5-star EDGE listed 6-5 / 240 out of Desert Edge (Goodyear, AZ) — national blue-chip with Florida in the live chase mix.
angle: Top-tier EDGE length with chase traits Florida can develop into a starter-upside rusher.
insiderNotes: Watched Desert Edge sophomore tape. George wins with length + chase first; next step is counters and staying low through contact.
